scope: repo-local; semantic review, not business-test or billing proof

initialReviews.review: D6 now separates reported/confirmed use, persistent dedup and member archives. Tasks 6.1-6.3 explicitly cover those responsibilities, including paid explicit curation rather than a timer.

initialReviews.target: requirement:skill-maintenance:Requirement: Maintenance results are durable and visible
initialReviews.review: D6 adds bounded display journals without losing cumulative history and resumable member operations. The durable-results requirement still demands changed/pending/conflict/failed and recovery visibility; archives and applying curation retain those states.

D6 permits only explicit budgeted semantic curation. The curation requirement retains list/propose/apply and forbids name-only deletion; registered curation tests exercise exact approval and restore of absorbed content.

D6's statistical contract is reflected explicitly in the expanded requirement: reported versus confirmed, persisted fingerprints beyond 4096 receipts, and statistics failures not disabling reading or pin.

D4 adds precise approval/content guards but retains real per-member transactions. The durable-writes requirement is only relocated and still forbids fictitious all-file atomicity or rollback; partial-member and recovery tests match it.
D4's content gate is represented in managed-ownership wording: ownership evidence is necessary, not sufficient; unknown prose/assets become bounded pending and pin/read-only remain independent.

D4's installed authority and content checks remain separate in this requirement. Its global-grant scenario now explicitly says unverified content stays pending; RPC cannot supply the specified TUI authorization.

D4's proposal/permission expansion does not widen project/global scope. Explicit-generation-scope remains unchanged: project-specific knowledge stays project and promotion must be requested; scope-migration tests enforce it.

initialReviews.target: requirement:skill-reflection:Requirement: Independent operation and shared charging
initialReviews.review: D7 changed position only. The independent/shared-charging requirement still means compatible participants share one request and own their writes; cooperation tests prove the protocol-double contract, not current memory runtime compatibility.

D7 is relocated without changing the contract. Task 7.1 permits a protocol peer double, 7.2 checks fees, and 7.3 remains unchecked while traceability is being completed; no real-memory compatibility is asserted.
D6's independent pin policy and evidence-based maintenance preserve this protection requirement. Rare/no-recorded-use is not deletion authority; activity and curation tests reject protected targets.

D4's new content approval does not replace version checks. The relocated read-before-mutation requirement still rejects stale targets without paid repair; proposal and commit-gates tests cover identity/hash and source changes.

D6 specifies member-bounded archive, shared-reference retention and no purge. The relocated reversible-archive requirement still forbids overwriting newer human files; archive and rollback tests verify conflicts and restoration.

D4 allows assets only through validated local writers. Installation-is-not-generation is relocated, not weakened: scripts/dependencies are recorded but never executed or installed by the skill writer.

Proposal scope now includes SDK final-source callbacks and unverified-content pending. D1 still routes these through public Pi extension APIs and narrow local modules; no fork, companion import or core modification was introduced.

D4's current ownership, exact approval and partial-write recovery map to tasks 4.2-4.4; task 4.1 separately covers scope. Installed approvals and interrupted recovery are tested, not inferred from intent metadata.

D6's merge/archive rules preserve scope and evidence. Scoped-knowledge wording is only relocated; repeated lessons update the existing ID instead of date-named references, as curation tests demonstrate.

D5 is relocated only. Task group 5 continues to cover full effective snapshot, settled-only scheduling, one-request proposals/content pending, and cancellation; the new cooperation hook reuses that path.

Expanded ownership/content requirements are discharged by tasks 4.2 and 4.3 together with 5.3. Ownership provenance never certifies arbitrary prose, and the installed grant cannot bypass content pending.

initialReviews.source: requirement:skill-maintenance:Requirement: Maintenance results are durable and visible
initialReviews.review: The durable maintenance-result requirement is relocated under expanded D6. Task 6.3 and 6.2 now cover persistent archive/member/applying state and explicit local recovery; model costs remain on the original review receipt.

Reviewable curation remains explicit and metered after relocation. Task 6.2 includes deterministic free candidates and one-request semantic proposal followed by exact local apply, not scheduled paid cleanup.

initialReviews.source: requirement:skill-discovery:Requirement: Explicit loading and native fallback
initialReviews.review: Explicit loading/native fallback changed coordinates only. Task 3.4 still covers stable-ID load, refresh and native restoration; modes tests and the plugin-unloaded native capture retain standard SKILL.md discovery.

initialReviews.target: requirement:skill-reflection:Requirement: Disable means no automatic model calls
initialReviews.review: D5 moved without a new fee policy. Disable-means-no-automatic-calls remains unchanged; disable cancels and persists off, and the registered fee matrix emits compaction/shutdown with zero provider calls.

The proposal additions propagate through unchanged D1 to task 1's public API/fake-provider checks. Task 1.4 remains a bounded historical observation, not new paid authorization or proof of current model quality.

Installation-is-not-generation is only relocated. Task 4's writers retain bytes and dependencies without executing scripts; source resolution skips missing packages and temporary resolution is offline.

initialReviews.target: requirement:skill-reflection:Requirement: Validated proposals and no recursive work
initialReviews.review: D5's one-request review is unchanged by relocation. The expanded validated-proposals requirement adds host templates/attributed source content and local exact pending approval; none adds a verification request.
Explicit-generation-scope wording did not change with D4. Task 4.1 still requires scoped copy/promotion, selected project root and conflict checks; approvals do not expand a target to global.
Scoped-knowledge wording is relocated under D6. Task 6.2's repeated-lesson update and same-scope curation checks preserve existing applicability; no mtime threshold or diary append policy was added.

initialReviews.source: requirement:skill-discovery:Requirement: Complete CLI and SDK source snapshots
initialReviews.review: The source-snapshot requirement now covers current restore permission for missing archived paths. Task 3.1's source callback plus task 6.3's restore path supply it; restore-source matrix rejects current exclusions and identity rebinding.

Reversible-archive wording moved only, while D6 clarifies member scope. Task 6.3 tests exact bytes/owner/ID recovery, shared references staying in place and refusal of subsequent edits; it does not implement purge.
Version-aware-read wording moved without relaxing freshness. Tasks 3.1/3.3/3.4 retain hash/version reads, refresh and source-error clearing; changed files cannot be served as a successful old read.

initialReviews.target: requirement:skill-reflection:Requirement: Isolated lifecycle and stale-result rejection
initialReviews.review: D5 relocation does not alter stale-result policy. The lifecycle requirement still withdraws old writers on input/tree/project/reload/shutdown; lifecycle tests preserve one old usage record without target writes.

D5 relocation keeps the one-request/default budget contract. Admission requirements remain unchanged: full snapshot, explicit skip, no retry/fallback; ledger and review-limits tests exercise these gates.

initialReviews.source: requirement:skill-reflection:Requirement: Independent operation and shared charging
initialReviews.review: Shared-charging requirement is relocated, not reduced. Task 7.1's permitted protocol double now exercises simultaneous targets, one disk record and separate commits; existing memory incompatibility is explicitly documented.

Installed-mutation requirement now states that global write permission cannot bypass content checks. Task 4.3 tests TUI exact diffs, RPC pending and grant revocation; task 5.3 provides the independent content gate.

Durable-writes requirement is relocated under updated D4. Task 4.4 retains before/after members and real committed state, rejects fake abort after commit, and recovers locally without another model call.
D5 moved only. Settled scheduling still separates user versus tool-bearing turns and excludes start/compaction/exit billing; scheduling tests cover three user turns and forty tool loops.
File-containment requirement moved only. Task 3.3 still rejects traversal and symlink escape and pages one requested file; read tests also demonstrate that viewing a script does not execute it.

D5 relocation does not expand learning-quality claims. Usefulness requirement still separates saved/reused from skipped/no-proposal and requires new authorization for extra real tests; evidence pages state those limits.

The expanded evidence requirement explicitly needs historical dedup and independent pin despite statistics failure. Task 6.1 and activity tests cover reported/confirmed separation, over-4096 replay and failed statistics with continued reading.

Read-before-mutation wording moved only. Task 4.2 retains exact SkillId/member read credentials and writer-time source/version checks; user-pasted hashes and same-hash different identities remain rejected.

initialReviews.target: requirement:skill-reflection:Requirement: Failures and usage remain visible
initialReviews.review: D5's position changed, not its visibility promise. Failure/usage requirement still retains unknown usage and persistent pause; fee-matrix and native failure/delivery evidence show status surviving reload.

D5 relocation propagates to unchanged task group 2. Its existing budget, accounting and TUI obligations remain met; late-over-reservation handling was added under the original overshoot rule, not memory's new R2.
Protection wording moved under D6. Task 6.1's pin and task 6.2's candidate eligibility keep user-owned/read-only/pinned targets protected independent of usage or file time.

D5 relocation keeps the effective-current-snapshot policy. The snapshot requirement remains unchanged: compressed projection rather than all raw history or an incremental substitute; snapshot tests verify deep-copy isolation.

Task 4 now includes installed/content/recovery additions, but scope.ts remains responsible only for trusted root selection and containment. scope-migration tests cover explicit roots/worktrees; mutation authorization stays in store/permissions, not this helper.

Discovery propagation reaches index.ts's real source refresh, explicit load and mode handlers. They use catalog identity/version checks, retain native fallback on error and never infer missing SDK source permission.

This is the second historical tasks:3→entry link, retained rather than deleted. The same registered status/refresh/load/mode handlers satisfy the relocated discovery obligations; no extra capability is claimed by the duplicate edge.

Discovery changes are reflected by sources.ts final-allowed snapshots, runtime noSkills handling and offline skip-only resolution. Missing-path restoration is separately implemented in restore-sources.ts, not guessed by ordinary discovery.

initialReviews.source: requirement:skill-reflection:Requirement: Validated proposals and no recursive work
initialReviews.review: Expanded validated-proposals requirement maps to task 5.3's source/template gate and bounded exact approval. Content tests reject execution claims and preserve request usage when locally approving pending content.

initialReviews.source: requirement:skill-reflection:Requirement: Isolated lifecycle and stale-result rejection
initialReviews.review: Lifecycle requirement received only propagated D5 relocation. Task 5.4 still covers actual input/navigation/reload and retirement of the old SDK session before another project; no arbitrary OS kill guarantee was added.

initialReviews.source: requirement:skill-reflection:Requirement: Disable means no automatic model calls
initialReviews.review: Disable requirement was relocated only. Task 2.4's enable/disable/pause UI and the new fee-matrix disable→compaction/shutdown case demonstrate no hidden request; native delivery verifies persistent OFF.
Admission requirement received only D5 relocation. Tasks 2.1/2.2 retain atomic reservation, limits and no fallback; joint boundary metadata adds dedup attribution, not new budget or retries.

Usefulness requirement moved without new real-test authority. Task 1 distinguishes deterministic closure from four historical SWE-2 observations; revised evidence explicitly says current content/cooperation changes were not paid-retested.

Discovery propagation maps to catalog.ts's allowed-source set, identity-aware search/view and bounded paging. Failed sources clear the index; native-mode behavior remains in index.ts and is tested separately.

The tasks:3→store edge covers generated-source provenance and version-aware updates, not discovery authority. Store validates known roots/member versions and index passes current-source authorization; it does not rescan excluded directories.

initialReviews.source: requirement:skill-reflection:Requirement: Failures and usage remain visible
initialReviews.review: Visibility requirement was unchanged by D5 relocation. Tasks 2.3/2.4 retain reported usage, unknown reservation and persistent pause; registered TUI matrix demonstrates no-change/empty/disconnect/cancel after reload.
Scheduling wording did not change under the moved D5 section. Task 5.2's distinct counters and settled-only eligibility still exclude repeated events and background reads from new paid work.

Current-snapshot requirement was only relocated. Task 5.1 captures effective projected entries/system/model and read versions without mutating the primary session; task 5.4 handles later invalidation.

Task 4's newer authority and member recovery obligations are implemented in store.ts: provenance/read versions, per-member checks, saved approval records and conflict-aware local recovery. Installed/content/rollback tests cover the added paths.

This second historical tasks:3→catalog edge carries the same allowed-source, freshness and containment responsibilities as the other edge. It is independently acknowledged, not silently removed or counted as extra testing.

Task 2 received position-only policy propagation. withLock remains the same local FIFO/exclusive-file primitive used for atomic admission; it does not schedule or enable requests, so disabling requires no lock redesign.

Task 1's usefulness propagation reaches index.ts's registered search/view/manage and review controls. Learning tests execute proposal→save→search/read reuse through these entries; invalid source snapshots still preserve native access.

Task 1 usefulness propagation does not change context.ts semantics. Its public projection/evidence snapshot is the common input for finite-template learning and reuse tests; it is not a claim of final-wire/cache parity.

Task 2's unchanged fee/disable policy maps to UI persistent controls. registerReviewUI cancels on disable, persists auto=false, subscribes to the ledger and does not release unknown reservations on resume.

Task 5 now includes content pending and full lifecycle guards. UI launch supplies currentness/source authorization to review, settled counters avoid duplicate work, and optional cooperation reuses—not bypasses—that launch path.

Task 1 usefulness propagation maps to store submit/save: evidenced template proposals are saved and then actually read in learning tests. Free prose may now be pending; historical SWE-2 evidence was qualified rather than treated as a current guarantee.

Task 2's unchanged budget rules are enforced by ledger.ts atomic admit/finish. New boundary/target attribution does not change unknown carry; overshoot after late telemetry re-pauses under the existing R2 requirement.

Task 1 learning closure uses catalog discovery/read of newly saved rules. Learning and automatic-learning tests read the resulting stable ID; search remains local and does not create a review request.

Task 2's request/usage duties map to reviewSkills: maxRetries=0, no tools, one stream, deadline/late-usage handling. Peer instruction bytes join the same input estimate and peer failure does not issue a correction call.

Task 2 received no semantic change from D5/disable relocation. atomicJson remains the fsync/rename persistence primitive used by ledger; it neither grants budgets nor schedules work and needs no behavior change.

Ledger added joint-boundary metadata and late-overshoot pause. ledger.test.ts now races two processes with different goal digests at one boundary, checks reload dedup, and tests late overshoot after resume; original crash/corruption/date cases remain.

UI changed optional coordination while retaining standalone scheduling. automatic-learning.test.ts still drives ten real tool turns, saves one rule and reuses it on a later task; source/budget/new-input negatives remain passing.

Review now combines participant signals but awaitWithAbort still only ends the controlled await, not the producer. Its promise rejection/late-handler cleanup contract matches usage-only late settlement and explicitly does not claim OS I/O termination.

New index handlers do not remove explicit load or native mode. modes.test.ts retains zero-request ID loading, live refresh and native completion/reload/disabled-plugin checks; native delivery independently confirms discovery after unload.

Catalog added activity/curation/impact methods without weakening view containment. read.test.ts still verifies requested-file paging, traversal and symlink rejection and non-execution of script assets.

Review's joint option is optional; test/learning.test.ts still exercises the existing standalone service and registered reuse. The initially failing stale-result regression was fixed by preserving its established late-accounting semantics, not changing its assertion.

Index additions preserve the official extension entry and prompt-section boundary. bootstrap.test.ts still loads the public factory, verifies zero startup calls and other system sections, and checks isolated snapshot behavior.

Index's CLI default entry still uses official source resolution. cli-sources.test.ts executes the stock CLI and registered tools with duplicate names/noSkills under isolated HOME, rather than mocking source decisions.

UI now has scheduling and target labels; the old TUI page incorrectly said scheduling was still absent. It was revised to label its 2.4 historical scope and link current fee/delivery evidence; old captures are not claimed as a new UI run.

Review adds classified peer results without removing single-stream protections. review-limits.test.ts still asserts maxRetries=0/no executable tools, bad/empty/reasoning outputs, partial usage, deadline, late settlement and budget skip; cooperation has separate added cases.

Catalog's maintenance additions do not change bounded search. search.test.ts continues to check 3000 skills, serialization budgets, stable pagination and zero model calls; protected curation filtering is separately tested.

UI's new coordinator preserves old fee controls. ui.test.ts explicitly keeps unknown reservations through acknowledgment/retry and survives a failing subscriber; new fee-matrix tests supplement it with registered TUI/reload cases.

Review's content policy has tightened since the four SWE-2 calls. swe2-validation.md was corrected to call them historical, require new authorization for rerun and disclaim current free-prose autosave/quality; no real request was made during this Adapt review.

Catalog now records activity and known references, but sources.test.ts still validates distinct IDs, owners, exclusions, empty sets, refresh failure and native fallback. Added maintenance behavior does not reinterpret user-owned files as managed.

UI added optional peer coordination; scheduling.test.ts still demonstrates 3 users/40 tool turns and duplicate settled events do not inflate counters or repeat a snapshot. Simultaneous peer declarations are covered by cooperation.test.ts, not attributed to this older test.

The source tests retain the documented loader/resolver distinction, final-allowed callback and source-failure fallback. source-discovery-boundary.md remains explicitly a 3.1 slice, not a claim that it alone proves maintenance or all learning behavior.

The review cancellation propagation still uses unchanged awaitWithAbort. Store waits only on controlled authorization and checks currentness per member; commit-gates/recovery tests demonstrate lock release and no late continuation, without asserting the callback producer was killed.

Bootstrap's entry behavior remains tested. implementation-evidence.md now reports the 160-test checkpoint, lists separate content/lifecycle/maintenance/cooperation evidence and clearly leaves final traceability pending; it does not infer model quality from bootstrap.

SDK source cases use support.ts's explicit final source callback and isolated auth/agentDir. Its new usage/price hooks only drive fake billing outcomes; they do not broaden allowed sources or load companion/personal extensions.

The CLI source fixture remains an observer/fake-provider harness for the stock CLI. Production source authorization stays in index/sources; no fixture hook bypasses noSkills or enables package installation.

Store's additional authorization/content paths retain commit gates. commit-gates.test.ts checks generation/path changes, same-root locking and source withdrawal; installed-specific grant/content cases are additionally linked through permissions/content tests.

Store now revalidates installed recovery grants and approved bytes. recovery.test.ts retains actual member/provenance/hand-edit interruption checks; installed-approval and rollback tests supply the new installed authority negatives rather than overclaiming the old test's scope.

Store's curation/rollback additions reuse existing member receipts and backups. member-transactions.test.ts still verifies real partial commit state, retained before bytes and assets without script execution; archive/rollback tests cover the new higher-level operations.

closingReviews.review: Only task 7.3's completion marker changed. fee-matrix.test.ts is byte-identical to the reviewed 160-test checkpoint; its request/unknown/crash assertions do not change when delivery is marked complete.
Only the delivery completion marker changed. The guarded command-only native fixture is unchanged and was used in the recorded isolated CLI run; no provider behavior or approval bypass was added.

Task 7.3 now records the operation chain and traceability already performed. delivery-evidence.md's exact commands, zero-call marker and file-access observations are unchanged; its limitations remain explicit.

The completion marker does not amend the protocol. cooperation.ts is byte-identical to its independently reviewed implementation; optional participation and incompatible-peer pause do not acquire real-memory compatibility from task completion.

Propagation is only the completed delivery marker through unchanged cooperation. review.ts remains identical: one stream, classified target callback and guarded separate commits; no new request path is introduced.
Propagation is only completion metadata. ledger.ts bytes, policy and joint-boundary admission are unchanged, including unknown carry and late overshoot pause; no R2/R5 synchronization is implied.
The cooperative tests are unchanged and still prove a protocol double, not the current memory runtime. Completing delivery does not widen that assertion or require an additional model call.

The native fixture is unchanged; the downstream evidence still describes the observed isolated run, not an arbitrary installation. No new screenshot or personal-data guarantee is inferred from the completion marker.
The delivery report is unchanged. usage.md retains the command/recovery workflow and explicit current-memory incompatibility; no installation or enabling action has been performed for the user.
The fee tests and their report are unchanged. fee-matrix.md keeps fake/SDK usage distinct from real bills, identifies the original-R2 overshoot fix and retains its historical native-UI boundary.
